senses.gloss: (b. h.; √בח, cmp. √בה s. v. בהי) [1) to be disordered, sick; whence בּוֹחַל q. v.].—2) (denomin. of בּוֹחַל) to be in that stage of ripening when the fig is called boḥal; cmp. בָּאַשׁ.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Maasrot 1:2">Maasr. I, 2</cite>) <he>התאנים משיִבְחֲלוּ … משילבינו וכ׳</he> figs are subject to tithes from the time they are called boḥal, which R. … defines, from the time their heads grow white.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sheviit 4:7">Shebi. IV, 7</cite> <he>בִּיחֲלוּ וכ׳</he> (Y. ed. <he>בִּיחֵילוּ</he>). Y. ib. 35ᵇ bot.; Y. Maasr. I, 48ᵈ (<cite ref="H00899"><he>חִיְּתָה</he></cite>) <he>מאי ביחילו חִיְּיתָה וכ׳</he> what is biḥ.? It (the fig) creates aversion (v. <cite ref="H00495"><he>חוּת</he></cite>), as we read (<cite ref="Zechariah 11:8">Zech. XI, 8</cite>) &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Maasrot 1:2">Maasr. I, 2</cite> <he>משיַבְחִילוּ</he> (Y. ed. <he>שביחילו</he>), v. supra. [Cmp. <cite ref="B00794"><he>בָּכַר</he></cite> as to spelling in Talm. Y.]
